change_summary: The tracked paper has been withdrawn, and its full text has been replaced by a withdrawal statement. The statement says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the results cannot be relied on. All the findings rest on those records, including the 2.1 °C lower peak indoor temperature, the 41% fewer hours above 28 °C, and the widening of the gap on hotter days. Anyone citing it should stop relying on these findings.
evaluation: Your draft takes its key green-roof parameter, the 2.1 °C cut in daily peak indoor temperature, from Okafor et al. [14] (Section 2.2). It then relies on that value in the Discussion and Conclusions. The paper has been withdrawn because its indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration. The 2.1 °C figure therefore can't be trusted, and your estimate of about half the person-hours avoided, the comparison with reflective coatings and the programme recommendation all depend on it. This is high impact. You will need a replacement value, or to rerun the model and the sensitivity analysis, before the draft can go further.
recommendation: Okafor et al. [14] has been withdrawn because its indoor temperature records were mis-calibrated, and your model's key 2.1 °C parameter comes from it. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, replace the value, rerun the model and sensitivity analysis, and re-check the Discussion and recommendation before the draft goes further.
